I have a complete picture. Here are my findings.

## Summary

**Redis is NOT used anywhere in this repository.** This is the Go project `usememos/memos`. There are zero matches for `redis`, `ioredis`, `REDIS_`, redis client imports, or connection URLs in any source file, `go.mod`/`go.sum`, `scripts/compose.yaml`, `scripts/Dockerfile`, docs, or the `web/` frontend `package.json`. There are no `.env`/`.env.example` files at all. The `scripts/compose.yaml` exists but contains no Redis service (only the memos app).

What exists instead is a **custom, hand-rolled in-memory TTL cache** (plus a few smaller ad-hoc caches). Note: `golang-lru/v2` appears in `go.sum` as a transitive dependency but is **not imported or used** anywhere in the source.

## 1. Redis
Not present. Explicitly confirmed absent across code, dependencies, config, compose, and docs.

## 2. The caching layer

### Primary cache implementation (in-memory, custom)
`/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go` — a thread-safe in-memory cache built on `sync.Map` + `atomic.Int64`, with TTL, a background cleanup goroutine, and max-item eviction. Key pieces:
- `Config` struct with `DefaultTTL`, `CleanupInterval`, `MaxItems`, `OnEviction` (lines 41-54).
- `DefaultConfig()` (lines 57-64): `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000`.
- `item` struct carries per-entry `expiration time.Time` (lines 34-39).
- `Set` uses default TTL; `SetWithTTL` sets `expiration: time.Now().Add(ttl)` (lines 92-120).
- `Get` lazily evicts if `time.Now().After(itm.expiration)` (lines 135-144).
- `cleanupLoop`/`cleanup` periodically purge expired items; `cleanupOldest` evicts ~20% when over `MaxItems` (lines 199-313).

### Cache wiring in the Store
`/bench/repo/store/store.go`:
- Three cache instances held on the `Store` struct (lines 27-29): `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`.
- Cache config defined inline in `New()` (lines 40-45): `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000`, `OnEviction: nil` — same values as `DefaultConfig()`. All three caches are created with this same config (lines 51-53) and closed in `Store.Close()` (lines 74-76).

### Other, smaller caches (not Redis, all in-memory / on-disk)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/instance_stats.go:21` — `instanceStatsCacheTTL = 60 * time.Second`; a single-value mutex-guarded struct `instanceStatsCache` with an `expiry time.Time` field (lines 23-44), used by `GetInstanceStats` (lines 59-67). Wired in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:43-44`.
- `/bench/repo/server/router/rss/rss.go` — an RSS feed cache: `defaultCacheDuration = 1 * time.Hour` (line 25), `maxCacheSize = 50` (line 26), a `map[string]*cacheEntry` with `createdAt`-based expiration (lines 34-48, 346-392) and a manual LRU eviction loop (lines 377-390).
- `/bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/functions.go:51-102` — a `sync.Map` (`regexpCache`) memoizing compiled regex patterns (no TTL).
- Disk-based derived-asset caches: `.thumbnail_cache` / `.motion_cache` folders (`/bench/repo/store/attachment.go:75-76`, `/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:32-36`).
- HTTP `Cache-Control` response headers only (not a data cache): `/bench/repo/server/router/frontend/frontend.go:24-104`.

## 3. TTL applied to user entries specifically

There is **no user-specific TTL**. User records inherit the shared 10-minute `DefaultTTL` from the store cache config. Details in `/bench/repo/store/user.go`:
- `userCacheKey(userID int32)` returns the user ID as a string (lines 88-90).
- `userCache.Set(...)` is called on create, update, list, and get (lines 98, 122, 132, 143, 167) — all via plain `Set`, so they use the default 10-minute TTL. There is **no** `SetWithTTL` call for users anywhere.
- `GetUser` reads from `userCache.Get` only when looking up by `find.ID` (lines 150-155).
- Cache invalidation on delete: `/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go:39-45` (`deleteUserCache` removes the user entry and its associated user-setting entries).
- Related user-setting cache keys: `/bench/repo/store/cache.go:7-9` (`getUserSettingCacheKey` → `"<userID>-<key>"`), used in `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go:59,78,86,106,122`.

`grep` for `SetWithTTL` across the codebase shows it is only defined and exercised in the cache package and its test (`/bench/repo/store/cache/cache_test.go:26`) — no production caller passes a custom TTL, so every store cache entry (users included) uses the default 10 minutes.

### Bottom line
No Redis, no external cache store, no configurable cache backend. Caching is entirely in-process: a custom TTL `sync.Map` cache in `store/cache/cache.go` (users, user settings, instance settings, all at a fixed 10-minute default TTL / 1000-item cap), plus a 60-second stats cache, a 1-hour RSS cache, a regex memoization map, and on-disk thumbnail/motion caches.
